Data pipelines that forecasters can trust: dbt, Airflow and data-quality testing

19 October 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer role at Brightwell Analytics (reference BW-DE-0417). Your forecasts depend on the nightly pipelines beneath them, and owning exactly that kind of platform has been my work for seven years, most recently at Tidewater Logistics in Rotterdam.

Your posting asks for production pipelines in Python and SQL, orchestrated with Airflow, with tested and monitored tables. This is what I have done, and what I would bring to your platform team:

- Pipelines at scale: I own the shipment-events pipeline at Tidewater, which moves 40 million events per day from Kafka into a PostgreSQL and BigQuery warehouse, orchestrated with Apache Airflow.
- Faster models with dbt: I cut the nightly rebuild of our delivery-performance mart from 6 hours to 55 minutes by moving it to incremental dbt models.
- Quality you can measure: I introduced Great Expectations tests on 30 core tables, and failed loads dropped 70 percent over two quarters.
- Growing engineers: I mentor two junior engineers and lead the weekly data-modelling review, which matches the design reviews you want your senior engineer to lead.

I should be open about one gap. I have not yet worked with Scala or Spark, which your heavy transformations use. My closest experience is the large Python and SQL transformations behind our warehouse, and I learn new tools quickly when a team needs them; I would plan my first weeks around closing that gap with your data scientists.

Your hybrid arrangement of two days on site in Amsterdam suits me well, since I live in Rotterdam and already commute within the Netherlands. I would be glad to walk you through the shipment-events design and hear how your forecasts consume your tables. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Alex Fernsby
